g.text: Idempotency and deduplication — and which guard is load-bearing
8 combinations, 3 outcomes: 23 lost · 45 correct · 67 doubled
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · total 45 · crash at event 4
TWO OPERATIONS, APPLIED TWICE
the distinction is about what the operation names, not about the data
once: 8 · twice: 8 — idempotent
ADD 8 to that window
once: 8 · twice: 16 — NOT idempotent
what makes the difference
SET names the RESULT; ADD names a change to whatever is there
so an idempotent sink needs
a value that does not depend on the sink's current contents
An accumulating pane (ch02) is a SET: it carries the window's whole total, so re-delivering it is harmless.
A discarding pane is an ADD: it carries only the delta, so re-delivering it double-counts. The accumulation mode decides whether your sink can be
idempotent at all.
Step 1/4 — idempotent means "twice is the same as once"
The test for idempotency is whether the operation names a result or a change. `SET = 8` is a result and survives any number of retries; `ADD 8` is
a change and does not. The note connects this back to ch02: accumulating panes are SETs and discarding panes are ADDs, so that choice decides
whether an idempotent sink is even possible.
Idempotency and deduplication — and which guard is load-bearing
8 combinations, 3 outcomes: 23 lost · 45 correct · 67 doubled
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · total 45 · crash at event 4
THE SHUFFLE RECEIVES THE REPLAY — ids 5, 6, 7, 8 ARRIVE A SECOND TIME
the receiver keeps every id it has accepted and drops repeats
records delivered to the shuffle
9 first time + 4 replayed = 13
the seen-set after the first pass
9 ids
replayed records recognised
4 of 4 — dropped
total reaching the aggregate
45 — correct
This requires the records to carry STABLE ids. A record whose id is generated at send time gets a new one on the retry, and dedup cannot see it.
And the seen-set is state: it grows with the number of records, so it needs its own bound — usually a window, which means dedup only works within
that window.
Step 2/4 — dedup at the shuffle: a set of ids already seen
Dedup at the shuffle is a seen-set and one membership test, and it works — 45, correct. The two things that make it not free are in the note: the
ids must be stable across the retry (a freshly generated id defeats it entirely), and the set itself is unbounded state that needs a horizon, so
dedup has a memory beyond which it stops working.

3 of the 8 rows reach 45. Read them: a replayable source is REQUIRED, and then dedup OR an idempotent sink is enough — they are redundant here.
Only three totals exist: 23 (lost), 45 (correct) and 67 (doubled). The source protects completeness; the other two protect accuracy.
Step 3/4 — the 8 combinations, and what each one actually produces
Worth reading carefully, because it refines the usual claim. "End-to-end exactly-once = source + shuffle + sink, drop any one and it breaks" is
not quite right for an aggregation: the source is load-bearing, and dedup and an idempotent sink are **redundant** — either alone reaches 45. The
next concept is where that redundancy disappears.
Idempotency and deduplication — and which guard is load-bearing
8 combinations, 3 outcomes: 23 lost · 45 correct · 67 doubled
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · total 45 · crash at event 4
WHY THE SOURCE IS DIFFERENT
the two accuracy mechanisms cannot create a record that was never re-read
what a replayable source gives
re-read from a committed offset — ids 5, 6, 7, 8 are available again
without it, after the crash
those 4 records are gone: total 23
can dedup recover them?
no — dedup only ever removes records
can an idempotent sink?
no — it only makes re-applying safe
Dedup and idempotency are both SUBTRACTIVE: they stop a contribution counting twice. Neither can add a contribution back.
So completeness has exactly one mechanism — replay — and accuracy has two. That asymmetry is why "replayable source" is the first requirement on
the list rather than one of three equals.
Step 4/4 — a replayable source is the one piece with no substitute
The asymmetry in the note is the practical takeaway. Dedup and idempotency are subtractive — they prevent double counting and can do nothing else
— so the only mechanism for completeness is a source you can re-read. If a source cannot replay, no amount of care downstream gets you past 23.
